title: Hidden behind the obvious: misleading keywords and implicitly abusive language on social media
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the prevalence of religion-targeted slurs alongside other demographic keywords (like ethnicity and gender) in abusive language datasets (AbuseEval, Davidson, Founta). It measured how the presence or absence of these explicit keywords affects a BERT classification model's ability to accurately detect implicit vs. explicit hate speech and offensive language.
findings: Religion was analyzed as one of the demographic topics for slurs. The study found that religion-related slurs had a very low frequency of occurrence in the AbuseEval, Davidson, and Founta datasets compared to general profanity, ethnicity, and gender-related slurs. The broader finding indicates that models struggle significantly to detect implicit abuse without explicit keywords (such as religious slurs) and often falsely flag non-abusive statements that happen to contain these keywords.
